topStories.headline: Australian-Style Handroll Shop Handroll Hawker Just Opened on Polk Street
topStories.dek: Melbourne native Romi Trower opened San Francisco's first Australian-style handroll restaurant at 2360 Polk St. on September 29, bringing grab-and-go temaki to Russian Hill.
topStories.body:
A new kind of sushi shop quietly joined the Polk Street corridor this week. Handroll Hawker, billed by its owner as San Francisco's first Australian-style handroll restaurant, opened Monday, September 29 at 2360 Polk St. in Russian Hill, in a former boba shop near Union Street.

The restaurant is the work of Romi Trower, a Melbourne native who moved to San Francisco in 2019 and, unable to find the snack she grew up on, decided to open it herself. The menu is concise: palm-size, cylindrical, uncut handrolls filled with spicy tuna, tempura shrimp, or salmon and avocado, along with miso soup and cold drinks. The format is designed for portability — rolls can be eaten at the counter, taken to go, or dropped into a paper bag for the walk home.

To run the kitchen, Trower hired chef Tai Trinh, who previously worked at Hayes Valley omakase counter Robin. Trower also traveled to Japan to attend culinary school in preparation for the opening. She brought in Flour + Water Hospitality Group as consultants to help with sourcing and permitting.

Handroll Hawker joins Saru just a few blocks away, giving Polk Street a rare concentration of dedicated handroll spots. The counter-service restaurant is open daily at 2360 Polk St., at the corner of Union.

topStories.headline: Chinatown's $150 Million Makeover Is Now Visibly Underway — and the Library Is About to Close
topStories.dek: With Portsmouth Square's pedestrian bridge already demolished and the Him Mark Lai Branch Library set to shut its doors this fall for a 30-month renovation, Chinatown is living through the most consequential construction period in a generation.
topStories.body:
Three major capital projects are simultaneously reshaping Chinatown's public infrastructure, and the effects are now being felt on the ground. Together, the Portsmouth Square renovation, the Chinatown Public Health Center upgrade, and the Him Mark Lai Branch Library renovation carry a combined price tag of roughly $150 million and will take up to two and a half years to complete.

The most visible change so far is the demolition of the Portsmouth Square pedestrian bridge — known for decades to skateboarders worldwide as 'China Banks' — which was torn down over the August 1–2 weekend. The 1971 structure had linked the square to the Hilton hotel across Kearny Street, but surveys found 77 percent of Chinatown residents favored its removal. Its demolition opened the first phase of the $73 million Portsmouth Square renovation, which broke ground in June and is expected to wrap in 2028. The finished square will include a new 8,300-square-foot community clubhouse, a larger playground, an adult fitness area, and an elevated performance stage.

The most immediately pressing development for residents is the Him Mark Lai Branch Library. According to the San Francisco Public Library and SF Public Works, construction is set to begin this fall — and the branch will close when it does. During the roughly 30-month renovation, library services will relocate to a temporary space at 950 Grant Ave., two blocks from the historic 1921 Carnegie building at 1135 Powell St. The renovation will restore the grand reading room to its original character, add a dedicated teen space, enlarge the community meeting room, and create a roof terrace.

Street closures and Muni reroutes related to the Public Health Center and Portsmouth Square projects began July 29 and are ongoing. Residents can check SFMTA.com/ChinatownParking for current traffic impacts.

topStories.headline: Fitness SF Polk Opens November 1 in the Long-Empty Lombardi Sports Building
topStories.dek: The locally owned gym chain has confirmed a November 1 opening date for its 45,000-square-foot Polk Gulch location at 1600 Jackson St., featuring the largest weight floor in San Francisco.
topStories.body:
After months of community outreach and a construction buildout, Fitness SF Polk now has a firm opening date: November 1, 2026. The gym will occupy 45,000 square feet at 1600 Jackson St. — the long-vacant former Lombardi Sports building at Polk and Jackson — serving Polk Gulch, Russian Hill, and Nob Hill residents.

The gym is billing itself around the city's largest weight floor and will be the only large gym in Northern California with an 18-piece Keiser A400 Circuit, a system used in professional sports facilities. Additional amenities include red light therapy, a traditional dry sauna, group fitness classes, and free parking — a notable feature for a dense urban location.

Fitness SF is a locally owned San Francisco chain. Founding memberships are currently on sale, and existing Fitness SF members with all-gym access will automatically gain access to the Polk location on opening day. Members can sign up at fitnesssf.com/location/sf-polk.

moreNews.headline: SF Planning Commission Advances City Bid to Acquire PG&E's Local Grid — Relevant After Summer Outages Hit Russian Hill and Chinatown
moreNews.body: San Francisco's Planning Commission unanimously approved a required Environmental Impact Report in July 2026 to advance the city's potential acquisition of PG&E's local distribution grid, according to Hoodline. The vote came amid a year of repeated major unplanned outages across the city — including an August 10 blackout that left more than 1,800 PG&E customers in Russian Hill, North Beach, and Chinatown without power for roughly an hour. The San Francisco Public Utilities Commission already generates about 75 percent of the electricity consumed in the city but does not own the physical grid that delivers it.

moreNews.headline: Lorella, a Bakery from the Octavia and Saturbake Teams, Is Coming to Polk Street
moreNews.body: A new bakery-café called Lorella is in the works at 2139A Polk St. in Russian Hill, according to The Infatuation's fall 2026 opening preview, published in late September. The project comes from the teams behind Octavia restaurant and Saturbake, a popular pop-up bakery. No opening date has been announced.
